title: Raúl Moreno, making stunning wines from sherry country
summary: Raúl Moreno is originally from Sevilla, and he began his wine education working in restaurants in London, where he moved
content:
Raúl Moreno is originally from Sevilla, and he began his wine education working in restaurants in London, where he moved to aged 18, beginning in the kitchen and then working as a sommelier. He then moved to Australia where he carried on working in restaurants, but also studied wine, doing a degree in wine science. This was followed by some vintages around the world: a great learning experience. Finally, he moved back home to Spain, where he has been working in the sherry area making brilliant unfortified wines. He began in 2017 with the Viñas Oceanicos wines all made in clay, but since 2021 has made wines under his own name

For more information on Raúl’s project, there’s a great article here: https://spanishwinelover.com/raul-moreno-brings-a-disruptive-vision-to-the-wines-of-jerez

Raúl Moreno Destellos 2024 Vino de la Tierra de Cadiz, Spain
From Pago Balbaina and Pago Miraflores. Palomino and Arinto, fermented and aged in 2000 litre sherry casks with no flor, 12 h on skins. 40 mg/l total SO2. lovely vivid tangy marmalade and lemon nose. Palate is focused and crystalline with beautiful citrus. So lovely. 95/100

Raúl Moreno La Morisca 2024 Vino de la Tierra de Cadiz, Spain
This is from 1959 plantings in Miraflores, 2 clones of Palomino, 12 months flor in chestnut then 9 months in steel. Complex, saline, intense nose. Lovely crystalline intensity on the palate. Salty with very subtle flor and nice spicy detail. Thrilling, with some phenolic characters. 96/100

Raúl Moreno La Angostura 2024 Vino de la Tierra de Cadiz, Spain
From 1945 plantings in Pastrana, Listran clone. More skin contact. 14 month flor in 300 litre French oak, then 6 months in stainless steel. Wonderfully expressive mineral citrus nose. Lovely concentration in the mouth lots of dry extract, mandarin, saline citrus, peach. Refined flor impact. Dry and fine. 96/100

Raúl Moreno La E Manzanilla NV Spain
This was a very commercial brand. But he’s making it without sulfites and no filtration. Youthful style no acid correction. Pure salty tangy flor nose. Fresh textural palate finishing warm and spicy. Lovely. 92/100

Raúl Moreno Aurora Manzanilla NV Spain
Average age 9 years light filtration no sulfites. Textured, complex, nice flor, warmly spiced but great length too. Beautiful. 94/100

Raúl Moreno La Esencia 2024
Many varieties, raised in qvevri, with some flor. Fresh, detailed, spice laden red cherry citrus has savoury spicy twist. Nice precision. Lovely. 94/100

Raúl Moreno Dark & Stormy 2024
Powerful and chunky but fresh and mineral with nice spicy intensity. So vital. Savoury twist on finish. 94/100

This was v cool!

title: Highlights: Sugrue Never Mind The Gamay Here’s The Pinot Meunier 2025 England
summary: Website: https://www.sugruesouthdowns.com/products/never-mind-the-gamay-2025 Sugrue Never Mind The Gamay Here’s The Pinot Meunier 2025 England12.5% alcohol. This blends together 97% Pinot Meunier
content:
Website: https://www.sugruesouthdowns.com/products/never-mind-the-gamay-2025

Sugrue Never Mind The Gamay Here’s The Pinot Meunier 2025 England
12.5% alcohol. This blends together 97% Pinot Meunier from Sandhurst Vineyard in Kent, with 3% Gamay from Robin Hutson’s Alpaca Block Vineyard at the Pig in West Sussex (Robin is an investor in Sugrue). It’s whole bunch ferment, and aged for four months in a mix of French and American oak. This is juicy and expressive with lovely red cherry and cranberry fruit supplemented by a twist of spicy oak. There’s a real poise to this wine, which shows massive drinkability but also has a touch of complexity and seriousness. It’s fun but not ephemeral, and I really like it. 92/100 (£29 from Sugrue directly)

title: Beaumes-de-Venise exploration: Domaine La Ligière
summary: Website: https://laligiere.fr/ I visited La Ligière with owner Philippe Bornard. This is his parents’ and grandparents’ estate. His father was
content:
Website: https://laligiere.fr/

I visited La Ligière with owner Philippe Bornard. This is his parents’ and grandparents’ estate. His father was selling grapes to the coops in Vacqueyras and Beaumes-de-Venise until 2008, which was Philippe’s first vintage.

He’s got 60 hectares of vines, of which 10 hectares make Beaumes-de-Venise, 30 hectares make Vacqueyras and then the remainder are Gigondas (0.5 hectares), Côtes de Rhône and Vin de Pays.

In addition, Ligière have a nursery business, and grafting was in full flow at the time.

Philippe has converted to organics, and has also stopped ploughing.

As a nursery owner, he has a good perspective on what is happening in vineyards around the region, and one thing he’s noticed is that vineyards seem to be dying after 30 years. There are lots of diseases, and lots of differences in yields.

‘We are now in the 2nd, 3rd and 4th generation of vines in some parcels,’ he says. ‘They use the same way of working, avoiding weeds by ploughing or using herbicides, all the time killing things to have clean vineyards. I think this is part of our problem: nature sees an empty space. Every time we kill something, it brings something else in.’

So he’s not killing his cover crops, but crimping them. ‘By not ploughing we reduced by about a third our tractor use, saving fuel and causing less compaction.’ 

Crimping the cover crop results in more space in the soil for worms and water.

They’ve also stopped exposing the fruit zone, and the wines are much fresher and brighter as a result. In the last couple of decades harvest has come from October to the beginning of September. So a change has been necessary. ‘My goal is that when you finish the first glass you want to go back for the second one,’ says Philippe.

A short film of the grafting process:

La Ligière Sud Absolu Blanc 2023 Vin de Pays Mediterranae, France
13% alcohol. Crisp and fresh with nice grapey fruit, showing good texture and a touch of herb and mint. Nice weight and freshness, with some texture. Expressive. With the Muscat he blends (this adds: sandy soils, clay soils and then sand and clay called gresse, and the combination is better than the individual terroirs, unlike the red).

La Ligière Les Garennes 2023 Beaumes de Venise
14% alcohol. Grenache, Syrah and Carignan from sandy soils. In concrete. This is rounded and supple with black cherry and blackberry fruit with some savoury spiciness and a bit of meatiness. So expressive with ripeness but also elegance. This is quite lovely. 93/100

La Ligière Muscat de Baumes de Venise ‘Chante Coucou’ 2023
15% alcohol. Blend of the three Muscat terroirs. Direct press, settle, then start fermentation, and the moutage is done at the last moment to have the minimum of sugar allowed (100 g/l with 10% tolerance), then add the alcohol in three stages. If you add the alcohol all at once it makes a distinct alcohol character in the wine that stays for longer. Fresh, tangy and grapey with some marmalade and mandarin notes as well as lemon and table grapes. Has nice freshness and acidity, with lovely purity. Nice complexity, too. 93/100

La Ligère Muscat de Baumes de Venise Chante Coucou Rosé 2024
15.5% alcohol. Red and white Muscat, pressed together. Rose petal, tea and herbs on the nose with some cherry and pear fruit. The palate is sweet and herby with nice strawberry and table grape notes, as well as some cherry. Supple, fresh and stylish with nice complexity and a bit of structure. So lovely. 94/100

La Ligère Muscat de Baumes de Venise 2014
15% alcohol. 8 years in barrel, without topping up, bottles in 2022. Muscat Blanc. Orange/gold colour. Spicy, grapey and rich on the nose with a hint of raisin and some spice. Rich, bold, spicy and intense on the palate with raisin, dried herbs. Lots of sweetness with amazing savoury, spicy presence. Quite lovely. 94/100

La Ligère Je Veux des Bulles Dans ma Vie! 2025
5.5% alcohol. Muscat, harvest 4 August at just below 10% potential alcohol, stopping fermentation at 5% by filtration, made in closed tank to keep bubbles, reinforcing these at bottling. Juicy and bright and grapey, with nice acidity and some sweetness. Light, easy but with good definition. Really enjoyable and bright. 88/100

title: Beaumes-de-Venise exploration: Xavier Vignon
summary: Xavier Vignon arrived in the region in 1996, and started to make wines here in 1998. He was an outsider,
content:
Xavier Vignon arrived in the region in 1996, and started to make wines here in 1998. He was an outsider, but it was standing above the village of Suzette, looking across to the Dentelles, where he decided he wanted to be a consultant winemaker focusing on the Rhône.

He is also one of the co-presidents of the Beaumes de Venise Cru. He took me to the spot high up in the cru where he looked over the vineyards back in 1996 and decided that this was the place for him.

Xavier made his name as a consultant, and his own wine project was born more-or-less by accident. During his consulting work, he took a little wine from each cru, just enough to make a small bottling (5000 litres = 1 pallet = 50 cases of 12). ‘This was my unit,’ he says. The idea was to demonstrate how good southern Rhône wines could be: back then, their quality wasn’t appreciated as much as it is now. He didn’t want to sell the wines, but rather he aimed to give them away.

But some friends of his submitted two bottles of each to the 2000 edition of the Guide Hachette, some 6 wines or so from each of 20 producers. They all ended up in the guide, and one from Ventoux got a coup du Coeur. His personal address in Barroux and his phone number was published in the guide, and it said that he was open 7 days a week (mistakenly; he wasn’t even selling wine). And people started turning up. ‘It became a nightmare!’ he says. But he registered as a negociant and began selling bottle by bottle.

Now he’s begun buying vineyards, too. This began when he sold his analysis laboratory in 2012. His focus is on Beaumes-de-Venise with 16 hectares, but he also has vineyards in Vaqueyras, Ventoux and Châteauneuf, with 37 hectares overall.

Xavier has some really interesting ideas, one of which is the Vinarium.

This is a large tank of 7000 litre capacity that acts like a sort of wine womb. Inside it, Xavier fits five 200 litre barrels, with stainless steel hoops and fittings (so they don’t corrode). He now has 10 Vinariums. Interestingly, there are two different sorts of Vinarium wine: the wine inside the barrels, and then the wine around the barrels – the amniotic fluid, if you like. I tried one white wine that was this latter category: it finishes fermentation in the tank (it goes to the Vinarium at 1030 density).

He’s also tried this with amphorae. He has one wine, a Châteauneuf-du-Pape, that he has aged for 6 years using this immersion process.

The story of how he devised the concept for the Vinarium is convoluted but interesting.

When he was running the analysis laboratory in conjunction with his consultancy work, he noticed that a lot of the tannins from the 2003 vintage reds were very dry. This was the very hot year, a couple of decades before almost all years were very hot. What could be done about these dry tannins?

In 2007 when he was consulting for Château La Nerthe, they tasted the 2003 and compared it with the new 2007 wine. The 2003 was tasting very dry, but the 2007 was tasting beautiful. The analysis was the same. He was trying to find a way to make the 2003 better: was there a way to soften those dry tannins?

Then, one night, he remembered an experience from 1988 when he was working in Saint-Emilion. He’d fined 400 barrels with albumin, but when he came back two weeks later and sampled the barrels, the tannins were still very dry. He didn’t understand why.

Then the old cellarmaster came in, drunk. He says that wines with hard tannins like these had happened many times, and the problem was caused by forgetting to add salt to the albumin. He added a gram of salt per hectolitre, and it was like a miracle.

So Xavier got up and went to the winery at 3 am in the morning, added 1 g salt/hectolitre in a bench trial. It was too much. But 0.2 g/hl worked like a treat. The hard tannins in the 2003 resolved, but salt isn’t a legal addition to wine, so he couldn’t say how he had turned the wines around.

He found a work around that was legal. The 2007 had much higher levels of mineral salts. Fives times as much. Adding 2007 to 2003 resolved the tannins. He published some studies on minerals and saltiness and their effect on tannins.

Xavier also did an examination of ageing barrels of wine in the sea. If there’s any exchange between the wine and the sea, then the wine is undrinkable. With wine in the sea, though, the oxidation process turned out to be much slower.

His sea immersion experiments were ended when he got in trouble with the customs, who fined him. His next trial was bringing the sea into the winery: he immersed barrels of wine in concrete tanks, but the concrete didn’t like the salt water.

This is where Xavier realised that it’s just liquid, and wine is a liquid. So this is where he began ageing barrels in wine, after changing the hoops to stainless steel from iron.

Xavier Vignon Extra Côtes du Rhône Blanc NV France
12.5% alcohol. This is a blend of three vintages of wine aged in the Vinarium, bottled in 2025. Grenache Blanc, Clairette, Piquepoul Blanc and Marsanne. 18 months on lees with low SO2, 24 months in Vinarium. This is really fresh and linear with lovely texture and good acidity. Pear, citrus fruit, pure and linear with great precision. Really interesting. 94/100

Xavier Vignon Beaumes-de-Venise 2022 France
15% alcohol. Aromatic, fine and pure with juicy red cherry and redcurrant fruit as well as fine spices. This is really elegant, wearing its alcohol well. Has real finesse, tending to elegance. 93/100

Xavier Vignon Arcane L’Etoile Beaumes de Venise NV France
15% alcohol. No vintage declared on this wine. Elegant and slightly peppery with layered cherry, strawberry and plum fruit. Rounded, with a bit of spicy framing and some silkiness, but also a bit of structure on the finish. Very stylish and quite intriguing. 93/100

Xavier Vignon Arcane L’Impératrice 2023 Gigondas, France
Warm, spicy, textural and elegant with strawberries and cherries, as well as some red fruit. Such precision and purity. 94/100

Xavier Vignon Muscat de Beaumes de Venise 2024
15% alcohol. Nice depth here with some layers of spice interweaving with the textured pear and grape notes. Rich but in balance, finishing sweet. 92/100

Video: touring around the cru with Xavier Vignon”

title: Beaumes-de-Venise exploration: Petitjean family, Domaine de Cassan and Château Les Croix des Pins
summary: Websites: https://domainedecassan.fr https://www.chateaulacroixdespins.fr Domaine de Cassan is a beautifully located estate at the foot of the Dentelles de Montmirail. I
content:
Websites: https://domainedecassan.fr https://www.chateaulacroixdespins.fr

Domaine de Cassan is a beautifully located estate at the foot of the Dentelles de Montmirail. I met with proprietor Jérôme Petitjean to hear the story and taste through the wines. As with many local domaines, he’s not restricted to just one cru, but has vineyards in three. As well as 4 hectares in Beaumes-de-Venise, he’s got 25 hectares in Ventoux and 7 in Gigondas.

The Domaine was established in the 1970s, and until recently was owned by the Croset family. In 2010 the Petitjean family took over running their vineyards in Gigondas and Beaumes-de-Venise, and converted them to organics. Two years ago they took over the domaine in its entirety. They are in the process of renovating the rest of the vineyards, where he says he’s got a lot of work to do.

The Petitjeans are originally from Epernay, and still have 5 hectares of vines in Champagne, as well as a two other domaines in Vaucluse: Croix des Pins and Domaine des Nymphes.

Château Croix des Pins also has some vineyards in Beaumes-de-Venise.

Domaine de Cassan Le Couer des Dentelles Beaumes-de-Venise 2024 France
15% alcohol. This is the main cuvée with 90% Grenache and 10% Syrah from vines at 400 m in clay/limestone soils. Aged in concrete tanks. This is supple and fine with sweet cherry and berry fruits, some silkiness and a hint of green. Easy and expressive. Fine-grained structure with lovely precision, carrying the alcohol well. 93/100

Château La Croix des Pins Les Contreforts de Montmirail 2024 Beaumes-de-Venise, France
15% alcohol. 80% Grenache, 20% Syrah, aged in concrete egg. There’s some nice black pepper and black cherry character here with sleek black cherry and blackberry fruit on the palate. This also has some saltiness and fine-grained structure. Fresh and expressive. 93/100

Domaine de Cassan Félibrige 2020 Beaumes-de-Venise, France
15% alcohol. 50% Grenache, 50% Syrah. Oak aged. Made by the former owner. This is rich, vivid and spicy with some tannic structure under the cherry fruit, with notes of liquorice and spice, as well as hints of pepper and olives. 93/100

Domaine de Cassan Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise 2024 France
15% alcohol. Fruity and aromatic with appealing grapey richness, and notes of pear and peach. There’s some melon, too. Lovely weight here: quite delicious. 93/100

title: The brilliant Douro wines of Mateus Nicolau de Almeida/Ameztoy & Almeida
summary: Website: https://ameztoyalmeida.com/ Mateus Nicolau de Almeida is the son of the well known João Nicolau d’Almeida of Ramos Pinto fame,
content:
Website: https://ameztoyalmeida.com/

Mateus Nicolau de Almeida is the son of the well known João Nicolau d’Almeida of Ramos Pinto fame, and the grandson of Fernando Nicolau d’Almeida who began Barca Velha back in 1952.

Growing up surrounded by wine he went out and got lots of experience around the world of wine, including an important time spent working on the Bordeaux properties of Denis Dubourdieu, the famous wine scientist. In 1996 he was working at Cantenac Brown, another Bordeaux estate, where he met his wife, Teresa Ameztoy.

Like Mateus, Teresa has a winemaking family background. Her father worked for La Rioja Alta, and she worked as chief winemaker at Ramos Pinto from 2005-2019, and now they both work together on the venture that Mateus began in 2014, after he left Muxagat, a winery he founded in 2003.

They have 4 hectares of organically farmed vineyards, and also source grapes from other growers.

Mateus Nicolau de Almeida Mater-Dôme (Mêda) Branco 2024 Douro, Portugal
Aged in a mix of concrete and 500 litre barrels. Lovely energy here. Bright and mineral with fine spices. Has nice citrus density and also some richer grapey notes. 93/100

Mateus Nicolau de Almeida Eremitas Antão do Desserto 2022 Douro, Portugal
Rabigato raised in concrete, after foot treading for 3 hours. Bold, mineral and spicy with nice density, and a bit of grip. Very stylish with nice weight. 93/100

Mateus Nicolau de Almeida Curral Teles Vinho Vermelho NV Douro, Portugal
A blend of 2020 and 2021, 3 hours foot treading then pressed. Nicely textured with sweet, smooth cherry and plum fruit. A lovely layered lighter red wine that’s soft and expressive. 93/100

Mateus Nicolau de Almeida Trans-Douro-Express Baixo Corgo 2022 Douro, Portugal
Aromatic with lovely sweet cherry and plum fruit. Some raspberry, too. Chalky and fine and fresh. 95/100

Mateus Nicolau de Almeida Curral Teles Tinto 2015 Douro, Portugal
This is stainless steel only. Rich but fresh, with lovely texture and finesse. Structured and broad but with real finesse. 95/100

Mateus Nicolau de Almeida Mater-Dôme (Mêda) 2009 Douro, Portugal
2 years in oak/concrete then 13 years in stainless steel. Fine and layered, spicy and dense, with a little evolution but lovely detail. Grippy and refined. 95/100

title: Sablière: a new 0% alcohol sparkling ‘wine’ designed from first principles
summary: Website: https://sabliere.co.uk/ I’ve written quite a bit about the attempts to make interesting, complex dealcoholized wines. There’s another approach, which
content:
Website: https://sabliere.co.uk/

I’ve written quite a bit about the attempts to make interesting, complex dealcoholized wines. There’s another approach, which is purpose-built proxies: complex non-wine drinks that operate in the same space as wine.

And this week I met up with Lucy Isles, co-owner of a new brand, Sablière, which is built from the ground up after a lot of research to behave just like a good Champagne or sparkling wine.

Lucy emphasizes that this is not a sparkling tea or a kombucha, but something that has been put together after a lengthy research journey.

Her partner in this venture is Kim Wilson, who studied brewing technology at Heriot Watt University, and then worked for Diageo. Sablière is made in their own facility in Edinburgh.

The challenge they faced is one that’s common to anyone working in the zero alcohol space. Without alcohol, they have no viscosity, no sterility, no mouthfeel and no texture.

She describes the research journey as a ‘wonderful multidisciplinary experience’.

They have worked with innovative South African winemaker Bruce Jack, with a microbiologist from Lallemand in Denmark, an Edinburgh University physicist looking at bubbles, and Andrew Gardner, a tea specialist (a tea specialist).

‘We were really trying to think, how can we do something novel here?’ says Lucy.

So, their first pair of sparkling wines are now live. These are meant to be wine replacements, and they are beginning to look at how they can also do this with still white and red wines.

The wines are built up using four key ingredients. There’s tea, which gives length. There are apples, for body. Honey gives aroma. And, finally, verjus gives acidity. They finish by carbonating to 6 bars pressure, the same as Champagne.

There are two expressions so far. One is a Blanc de Blancs style, which they based on Ruinart, and the other is a rosé based on Charles Heidsieck.

The Blanc is a blend of white teas, and they worked with tea sommelier Joyce Maina to select these. There are white curls from Nepal, and white peony from China. They extract the teas in house, using a different process for each. The verjus is from Sussex, which adds viscosity and acidity, and this is balanced with malic acid from cox apples. They use a range of yeasts from Lallemand to give some wine-like qualities, but this fermentation produces no alcohol.

One key decision was to go for 0.0% alcohol rather than 0.5% because of the Middle East market.

The final element is blossom honey distillate, adding sweetness but not sugary weight. Altogether the Blanc and Rosé have 37 g/l sugar. So they are sterile filtered. There are no added sulfites, but some sulfites are used by the verjus producer: they are looking to see whether they could eliminate these sulfites too.

What does it taste like? It has lovely aromas: fruity, herby and aromatic with some honeyed notes, floral elements and a touch of green. The palate is fresh and textured and you get the honey and tea notes, but also nice fruitiness and good acidity. Very stylish and fruit driven.

The rosé has Kentish kiss apples which give some pink notes. Four teas are used: mountain oolong (smoky, oxidized notes), gold curl, wild lapsang and da hong pao (delicate caramel).

It’s a golden colour with a slight pink hue. There’s a fruity, herby note on the nose with red apple, mandarin and dried herbs. In the mouth there’s nice bite with some structure and good acidity, and nice herby complexity. There’s even a slight caramel twist. This is really good.

I wouldn’t mistake either for Champagne, but these are high quality, intentional sparkling ‘wines’ that are quite friendly and offer a bit of complexity. Sablière are selling direct to customers at £32 for the Blanc and £35 for the Rosé. They launched quietly in January, their website was launched in April, and they already have 20 clients (restaurants and retail).

title: Highlights: the chillable Olivier Coste Bisou Rouge 2025
summary: This is great: a delicious, drinkable Languedoc red designed to be drunk chilled. Olivier Coste Bisou Rouge 2025 Pays d’Oc,
content:
This is great: a delicious, drinkable Languedoc red designed to be drunk chilled.

Olivier Coste Bisou Rouge 2025 Pays d’Oc, France
11.5% alcohol. This is designed to be served chilled, and the lips on the front label change from red to blue when it’s at the right temperature. It’s a lighter-style red with low tannins, but it’s still a red wine. Lovely floral, sappy, sweet cherry and berry fruits, and nice weight on the palate. Crunchy and delicious; fruity and enjoyable. There’s a touch of sweetness and it is juicy and easy, but satisfying. Really impressive. 91/100

title: The wines of Zacharioudakis, Crete
summary: Website: https://www.zacharioudakis.com/en/ Zacharioudakis is a family-owned winery from northern Crete, near Heraklion. It was started in 2000 by journalist Stelios
content:
Website: https://www.zacharioudakis.com/en/

Zacharioudakis is a family-owned winery from northern Crete, near Heraklion. It was started in 2000 by journalist Stelios Zacharioudakis, and since 2009 it has been his full time job. The 20 hectares of organically farmed vineyards are at an altitude of 500 metres, which tempers the hot climate.

Zacharioudakis Codex White 2024 Crete, Greece
In a striking white bottle. This is 80% Assyrtiko, 20% Muscat Spinas. Lively and bright with crisp citrus fruit. Tart, with some grapey detail. Nice purity here. 89/100

Zacharioudakis Assyrtiko 2023 Crete, Greece
13% alcohol. Dense with fresh lemony fruit and some pithiness. Has a bit of grip. 89/100

Zacharioudakis Orthi Petra 2024 Crete, Greece
A blend of Sauvignon Blanc and Vidiano. Crisp and bright with lemony fruit. Tart, showing nice intensity and some herby hints. 88/100

Zacharioudakis Vidiano 2023 Crete, Greece
5 months in French oak. Juicy, lively and bright with nice focus and a hint of mint, some herbs, and a nice acid line. Has a bit of structure. 90/100

Zacharioudakis Victoria Rosé 2024 Crete, Greece
70% Cabernet Sauvignon, 30% Kotsifali. Juicy and bright with some tartness. Bright red cherry and plum fruit with good focus and acidity. 88/100

Zacharioudakis Codex Red 2022 Crete, Greece
14% alcohol. In a black bottle. Syrah, Merlot and Kotsifali. Juicy, bright and fresh with a chalky mineral edge to the fruit. Nice purity. 90/100

Zacharioudakis Kotsifali 2021 Crete, Greece
14% alcohol. 8 months in oak. Lighter in colour, this is juicy and bright with good acidity. It’s fruity and expressive with a nice savoury twist. 92/100

title: Reynolds Wine Growers: top wines from the cooler north of Portugal’s Alentejo
summary: Website: https://reynoldswinegrowers.com/en/ Reynolds Wine Growers is a significant producer, with a 200 hectare farm in Figuera de Cima, with 40
content:
Website: https://reynoldswinegrowers.com/en/

Reynolds Wine Growers is a significant producer, with a 200 hectare farm in Figuera de Cima, with 40 hectares of vines. One of the benefits of the location is altitude, at 600 m. This is next to Serra de São Mamede Natural Park, Portalegre, in the north of the region. They also have two other smaller vineyards in other locations.

It’s currently being run by Julian Reynolds, whose grandfather, Thomas Reynolds, introduced Alicante Bouschet into Portugal. This is the same Reynolds family that was behind another Alentejo winery, Mouchão. I tasted these wines with Julian.

Yields are low at 3.5 tons/ha. They pick by variety, and don’t crush any of the grapes, just destem. Whites are fermented and aged in stainless steel, while reds are fermented in large oak, then do malolactic in barrel.

Reynolds Wine Growers Gloria Reynolds Art & Tradition Branco 2021 Alentejo, Portugal
This is Antão Vaz. Nice intensity on the nose, with pear and peach fruit. There’s lovely fruity depth on the palate with a spicy, savoury edge. Grainy and chiselled with a lovely fruit core. 94/100

Reynolds Wine Growers Alicante Bouschet Grande Reserva ‘Julian Reynolds’ 2016 Alentejo, Portugal
There’s a bit of Syrah in the mix here. Beautiful floral intensity on the nose, which is fine and sweetly aromatic. The palate has freshness and density with real elegance. Such purity, this is ageing really well, and has a long way still to go. 96/100

Reynolds Wine Growers Alicante Bouschet Grande Reserva ‘Julian Reynolds’ 2005 Alentejo, Portugal
Nice development on the nose with some iodine and spice. Quite mineral with sweet berry fruits. Has tannins still, and savoury notes of spice, earth and iodine. Fresh, mineral and complex with great intensity. Fully developed, but still alive. 95/100

Reynolds Wine Growers Gloria Reynolds Art & Tradition 2014 Alentejo, Portugal
100% Alicante, two years in Seguin Moreau Icône Elégance barrels. Concentrated and fresh, and still taut and focused, with blackcurrant and black cherry fruit with good density and tannins. Focused, with a firm, grippy finish. So lovely and full of interest. 95/100

Reynolds Wine Growers Gloria Reynolds Cathedral 2005 Alentejo, Portugal
They release 2000 bottles of this and keep the rest for friends and family. Alicante Bouschet. Still deeply coloured with a slight savoury edge to the nose. Earth, malt and soy sauce notes on the nose as well as vivid fruit. The palate is concentrated and dense with some nice grip. Bold and vivid with a savoury twist, and fully mature. 93/100

title: Bachelder revisited: tasting through the 2023s from this important Canadian producer, who is mapping Niagara one vineyard at a time
summary: It was great to take the opportunity to taste once again with Thomas Bachelder, one of Canada’s top winemakers. Geoffrey
content:
It was great to take the opportunity to taste once again with Thomas Bachelder, one of Canada’s top winemakers. Geoffrey Moss, Rhys Pender, Jeremy Bonia and I had been judging at the WineAlign National Wine Awards of Canada, and Thomas had lent us a couple of guitars for the week. When we returned them on the way to the airport, we stopped at the Bat Cave for a tasting, focusing on Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, but also bringing Gamay into play.

I’ve covered Thomas’ wines before in detail:

He originally made wine in three locations: Niagara, Burgundy and Oregon, which is quite a stretch. But in time, he began to see his mission as focusing on his home patch, in Niagara, and going deeper into terroir than perhaps anyone else has done before.

‘We were considered a Chardonnay producer rather than a Pinot producer,’ says Thomas, but he explained that if you have five hectares of each, you’ll be making much more Chardonnay than Pinot. This is because of the larger yields of Chardonnay, and the bigger yield in litres of wine per tonne of grapes (650 versus 550). And often to get the Pinot Noir, you have to take the Chardonnay, too.

We focused on 2023, when he made 9 Chardonnays and 10 Pinots. Thomas likes to taste across the Peninsula, starting off near the Niagara River (the border with the USA) and then heading west. Along the way, lots of factors influence the wines. Proximity to the lake is a big factor, and whether you are on the flats or on the bench. And soil type plays a role. ‘We are the new monks,’ says Thomas. ‘We have to figure out Niagara in real time.’ It’s exciting work diving into the sort of parcellation of site that is then reflected in the wines. And scale is an issue. For some of Thomas’ vineyard sources, he might separate out a few rows that are different, and bottle them separately.

For Pinot Noir he doesn’t use any whole bunch (he does with Gamay, extensively). Wild yeast ferments, no sulfites until after malolactic fermentation. And he only uses Burgundian barrels from Burgundian producers. Most of the wines have 20% new oak, but some have none.

What is remarkable about these wines is just how different they are. They are genuinely shaped by site.

PINOT NOIR

Bachelder Bator Pinot Noir 2023 Four Mile Creek, Niagara, Canada
12.5% alcohol. Sadly the Bator vineyard was ripped out in 2024, and so Thomas lost a classic Four Mile Creek source of Pinot, Gamay and Chardonnay. Fine clay ranging to sandy loam soils. No new oak. Aromatic, floral, raspberry, strawberry, showing some richness and intensity. Spicy, herbal, with nice precision. Has some warmth and spice. Lovely. 94/100

Bachelder Lowrey Pinot Noir Vieilles Vignes 2023 Saint David’s Bench, Niagara, Canada
12% alcohol. 1984, 1988, 1993, 1997 and 1999 plantings, nestled in the foot of the escarpment up against St David’s Bench. 20 months in new and used oak. Floral, fresh, silky and finely spiced. Lovely elegance here with sweet strawberry and cherry fruit. Supple, chalky and fine with redcurrant and cherry. So expressive with nice tensile tannins and acid. 95/100

Bachelder Old Eastern Block of Lowrey Pinot Noir 2023 Saint David’ Bench, Niagara, Canada
12% alcohol. Only the 1984 and 1988 plantings in this. 20 months in new and used oak. Floral and taut on the nose with redcurrant and strawberry notes. The palate is silky and fine with nice tension, showing sweet fruit with a bit of spicy tension. So layered and expansive. 95/100

Bachelder Wismer-Parke Pinot Noir 2023 Twenty Mile Bench, Niagara, Canada
13% alcohol. Planted 1999. 10 barrels. Red soils here: magnesium oxide and dolomitic limestone-influenced clay soils.. Supple and floral on the nose with red cherries and redcurrants. There’s some concentration here with bold black and red cherries, with a bit of grunt. Quite mineral and intense, but the fruit stays silky and layered. 95/100

Bachelder Wild West End of Wismer Parke Pinot Noir 2023 Twenty Mile Bench, Niagara, Canada
13% alcohol. Planted 1999. Four or five barrels. Very fine and floral on the nose with delicate, pretty, green-tinged cherry fruit. The palate is beautifully textured with delicacy and finesse. This has a beautiful purity and delicacy, and an amazing tapered finish. Such a lovely mouthfeel, with some chalkiness. There’s a finesse to this wine. 96/100

Bachelder Hanck Pinot Noir 2023 Twenty Mile Bench, Niagara, Canada
Hanck, which is just 20 metres north of Wismer-Parke Wild West End, is more regal, says Thomas. Planted in 2005, and owned by King and Victoria winery. There’s some warmth here with fine spiciness and some herbal hints. It’s warm, rich and has some stewed strawberry notes, finishing a bit spicy. Very likeable with sweet, rich fruit. 93/100

Bachelder Spencer-Morgan La Côte Nord Pinot Noir 2023 Vineland, Twenty Mile Bench, Niagara, Canada
At 175 m (this is as high as it gets in Niagara, in Vineland, this is Megalomaniac Winery’s best block. Lovely vibrant raspberry and cherry fruit with fine spices and some silkiness, framed with a bit of grunt and iron. So expressive, showing some mid-palate richness, but also a bright finish. Nice grainy detail, but the focus is on the sweet fruit. 94/100

Bachelder Ivy and Warren Saunders Parcelle ‘Haut’ 2023 Beamsville Bench, Niagara, Canada
12.5% alcohol. Organically farmed. Peppery and bright on the nose with some redcurrant and herb. It’s distinctive. Bright and peppery with tart redcurrant fruit and some cured meat savouriness, and even some blood and iron. Orange peel. 95/100

Bachelder Les Villages Bench Pinot Noir 2024
Fruity, direct, nice acidity, nice silky redcurrant and cherry fruit, with some salty notes, a touch of liqourice, and enough structure to frame the fruit. Such great balance to this wine. 94/100

CHARDONNAY

Bachelder Bator Chardonnay 2023 Four Mile Creek Niagara, Canada
No new oak. No limestone. Lovely weight and texture here. Pear, citrus, even a touch of peach. Nice layers of fruit with some ample pear and fig, but also some freshness. Stylish and quite broad. 93/100

Bachelder Cuesta Far East Man Chardonnay 2023 Twenty Mile Bench, Niagara, Canada
Lots of gritty dolomitic limestone. Fine and tensile with lemon and white peach, and a bit of grip. Nice acidity here. Tensile and refined with a grainy minerality. This is lovely and expressive with the limestone signature present. 95/100

Bachelder Wismer-Foxcroft Parcelle Nord 2023 Twenty Mile Bench, Niagara, Canada
So refined. Beautiful crystalline citrus aromatics with some honey and nut character alongside lemon and pear. A touch of oak, but also some lovely mineral character. Beautiful fruit expression here. Complete with some richness. 95/100

Bachelder Wismer-Wingfield Chardonnay 2023 Twenty Mile Bench, Niagara, Canada
Fresh and supple with nice tension to the pear and citrus. Has nice aniseed hints, with some fine herbs. Lovely acidity. Fine and pure. 95/100

Bachelder Hill of Wingfield Wismer Wingfield Vineyard Chardonnay 2023 Twenty Mile Bench Niagara, Canada
Focused and taut on the nose with lovely aromatics. Nice citrus and pear fruit as well as some white peach. Lovely fruit expression here. Good impact and weight. 94/100

Bachelder Ivy and Warren Saunders Parcelle Haut Chardonnay 2023 Beamsville Bench Niagara, Canada
Focused, fresh grapefruit and lemon on the nose. Some nice green hints. The palate has a slight saltiness, some sweet pear fruit too. Really distinctive. Finishes saline. 94/100

Bachelder Red Clay Barn Block of Grimsby Hillside Vineyard Chardonnay 2023 Lincoln Lakeshore, Niagara, Canada
Floral, fruit-driven and expressive. Bold and rich with bold, viscous pear, citrus and pear. Rich and textural with a touch of aniseed and sweet peachy notes. Lovely weight here. 94/100

Bachelder Frontier Block of Grimsby Hillside Vineyard Chardonnay 2023 Lincoln Lakeshore, Niagara, Canada
High limestone site, close to lake. Taut, refined aromatics. Lovely tension from the limestone. Beautiful citrus and white peach with real density. Real finesse and focus with tension as well as depth. Slightly salty on the finish. 96/100

GAMAY

Bachelder Baixu Gamay 2024 Four Mile Creek, Niagara, Canada
1981 plantings. 10% whole cluster. Little limestone. Supple and fresh with lovely red cherry and redcurrant fruit, showing lovely tension and directness to the fruit. This is really beautiful and expressive, finishing with a lovely tapering minerality. 95/100

Bachelder Haynes Street Gamay 2024 Creek Shores, Niagara, Canada
22% whole bunch. A vineyard near Jordan. Young vines, some limestone. Bench-adjacent. Lovely direct raspberry and cherry fruit. Nice density and fruit purity. Very fine. Lovely forward fruit here with volume and intensity. 94/100

Bachelder Wismer-Foxcroft Gamay 2024 Twenty Mile Bench, Niagara, Canada
25% whole bunch.  Older vines. Fresh, aromatic, floral red currant and raspberry nose. Peppery and pungent. Fine, expressive and lovely. Juicy and expressive, with some iron and blood and lovely tension and complexity. Grainy but such finesse. 95/100

title: Raúl Moreno, making stunning wines from sherry country
summary: Raúl Moreno is originally from Sevilla, and he began his wine education working in restaurants in London, where he moved
content:
Raúl Moreno is originally from Sevilla, and he began his wine education working in restaurants in London, where he moved to aged 18, beginning in the kitchen and then working as a sommelier. He then moved to Australia where he carried on working in restaurants, but also studied wine, doing a degree in wine science. This was followed by some vintages around the world: a great learning experience. Finally, he moved back home to Spain, where he has been working in the sherry area making brilliant unfortified wines. He began in 2017 with the Viñas Oceanicos wines all made in clay, but since 2021 has made wines under his own name

For more information on Raúl’s project, there’s a great article here: https://spanishwinelover.com/raul-moreno-brings-a-disruptive-vision-to-the-wines-of-jerez

Raúl Moreno Destellos 2024 Vino de la Tierra de Cadiz, Spain
From Pago Balbaina and Pago Miraflores. Palomino and Arinto, fermented and aged in 2000 litre sherry casks with no flor, 12 h on skins. 40 mg/l total SO2. lovely vivid tangy marmalade and lemon nose. Palate is focused and crystalline with beautiful citrus. So lovely. 95/100

Raúl Moreno La Morisca 2024 Vino de la Tierra de Cadiz, Spain
This is from 1959 plantings in Miraflores, 2 clones of Palomino, 12 months flor in chestnut then 9 months in steel. Complex, saline, intense nose. Lovely crystalline intensity on the palate. Salty with very subtle flor and nice spicy detail. Thrilling, with some phenolic characters. 96/100

Raúl Moreno La Angostura 2024 Vino de la Tierra de Cadiz, Spain
From 1945 plantings in Pastrana, Listran clone. More skin contact. 14 month flor in 300 litre French oak, then 6 months in stainless steel. Wonderfully expressive mineral citrus nose. Lovely concentration in the mouth lots of dry extract, mandarin, saline citrus, peach. Refined flor impact. Dry and fine. 96/100

Raúl Moreno La E Manzanilla NV Spain
This was a very commercial brand. But he’s making it without sulfites and no filtration. Youthful style no acid correction. Pure salty tangy flor nose. Fresh textural palate finishing warm and spicy. Lovely. 92/100

Raúl Moreno Aurora Manzanilla NV Spain
Average age 9 years light filtration no sulfites. Textured, complex, nice flor, warmly spiced but great length too. Beautiful. 94/100

Raúl Moreno La Esencia 2024
Many varieties, raised in qvevri, with some flor. Fresh, detailed, spice laden red cherry citrus has savoury spicy twist. Nice precision. Lovely. 94/100

Raúl Moreno Dark & Stormy 2024
Powerful and chunky but fresh and mineral with nice spicy intensity. So vital. Savoury twist on finish. 94/100

This was v cool!

title: Highlights: Sugrue Never Mind The Gamay Here’s The Pinot Meunier 2025 England
summary: Website: https://www.sugruesouthdowns.com/products/never-mind-the-gamay-2025 Sugrue Never Mind The Gamay Here’s The Pinot Meunier 2025 England12.5% alcohol. This blends together 97% Pinot Meunier
content:
Website: https://www.sugruesouthdowns.com/products/never-mind-the-gamay-2025

Sugrue Never Mind The Gamay Here’s The Pinot Meunier 2025 England
12.5% alcohol. This blends together 97% Pinot Meunier from Sandhurst Vineyard in Kent, with 3% Gamay from Robin Hutson’s Alpaca Block Vineyard at the Pig in West Sussex (Robin is an investor in Sugrue). It’s whole bunch ferment, and aged for four months in a mix of French and American oak. This is juicy and expressive with lovely red cherry and cranberry fruit supplemented by a twist of spicy oak. There’s a real poise to this wine, which shows massive drinkability but also has a touch of complexity and seriousness. It’s fun but not ephemeral, and I really like it. 92/100 (£29 from Sugrue directly)

title: Beaumes-de-Venise exploration: Domaine La Ligière
summary: Website: https://laligiere.fr/ I visited La Ligière with owner Philippe Bornard. This is his parents’ and grandparents’ estate. His father was
content:
Website: https://laligiere.fr/

I visited La Ligière with owner Philippe Bornard. This is his parents’ and grandparents’ estate. His father was selling grapes to the coops in Vacqueyras and Beaumes-de-Venise until 2008, which was Philippe’s first vintage.

He’s got 60 hectares of vines, of which 10 hectares make Beaumes-de-Venise, 30 hectares make Vacqueyras and then the remainder are Gigondas (0.5 hectares), Côtes de Rhône and Vin de Pays.

In addition, Ligière have a nursery business, and grafting was in full flow at the time.

Philippe has converted to organics, and has also stopped ploughing.

As a nursery owner, he has a good perspective on what is happening in vineyards around the region, and one thing he’s noticed is that vineyards seem to be dying after 30 years. There are lots of diseases, and lots of differences in yields.

‘We are now in the 2nd, 3rd and 4th generation of vines in some parcels,’ he says. ‘They use the same way of working, avoiding weeds by ploughing or using herbicides, all the time killing things to have clean vineyards. I think this is part of our problem: nature sees an empty space. Every time we kill something, it brings something else in.’

So he’s not killing his cover crops, but crimping them. ‘By not ploughing we reduced by about a third our tractor use, saving fuel and causing less compaction.’ 

Crimping the cover crop results in more space in the soil for worms and water.

They’ve also stopped exposing the fruit zone, and the wines are much fresher and brighter as a result. In the last couple of decades harvest has come from October to the beginning of September. So a change has been necessary. ‘My goal is that when you finish the first glass you want to go back for the second one,’ says Philippe.

A short film of the grafting process:

La Ligière Sud Absolu Blanc 2023 Vin de Pays Mediterranae, France
13% alcohol. Crisp and fresh with nice grapey fruit, showing good texture and a touch of herb and mint. Nice weight and freshness, with some texture. Expressive. With the Muscat he blends (this adds: sandy soils, clay soils and then sand and clay called gresse, and the combination is better than the individual terroirs, unlike the red).

Domaine La Ligière Les Garennes 2023 Beaumes de Venise
14% alcohol. Grenache, Syrah and Carignan from sandy soils. In concrete. This is rounded and supple with black cherry and blackberry fruit with some savoury spiciness and a bit of meatiness. So expressive with ripeness but also elegance. This is quite lovely. 93/100

Domaine La Ligière Les Garennes Beaumes de Venise 2024
14% alcohol. Organic. 60% Grenache, 40% Syrah. Slight meaty nose with some char notes, as well as bright berry fruits. The palate is vivid and substantial with rich berry and cherry fruit, with a spicy, structured finish. Rich style. 92/100

La Ligière Muscat de Baumes de Venise ‘Chante Coucou’ 2023
15% alcohol. Blend of the three Muscat terroirs. Direct press, settle, then start fermentation, and the moutage is done at the last moment to have the minimum of sugar allowed (100 g/l with 10% tolerance), then add the alcohol in three stages. If you add the alcohol all at once it makes a distinct alcohol character in the wine that stays for longer. Fresh, tangy and grapey with some marmalade and mandarin notes as well as lemon and table grapes. Has nice freshness and acidity, with lovely purity. Nice complexity, too. 93/100

La Ligère Muscat de Baumes de Venise Chante Coucou Rosé 2024
15.5% alcohol. Red and white Muscat, pressed together. Rose petal, tea and herbs on the nose with some cherry and pear fruit. The palate is sweet and herby with nice strawberry and table grape notes, as well as some cherry. Supple, fresh and stylish with nice complexity and a bit of structure. So lovely. 94/100

La Ligère Muscat de Baumes de Venise 2014
15% alcohol. 8 years in barrel, without topping up, bottles in 2022. Muscat Blanc. Orange/gold colour. Spicy, grapey and rich on the nose with a hint of raisin and some spice. Rich, bold, spicy and intense on the palate with raisin, dried herbs. Lots of sweetness with amazing savoury, spicy presence. Quite lovely. 94/100

La Ligère Je Veux des Bulles Dans ma Vie! 2025
5.5% alcohol. Muscat, harvest 4 August at just below 10% potential alcohol, stopping fermentation at 5% by filtration, made in closed tank to keep bubbles, reinforcing these at bottling. Juicy and bright and grapey, with nice acidity and some sweetness. Light, easy but with good definition. Really enjoyable and bright. 88/100

title: Beaumes-de-Venise exploration: Xavier Vignon
summary: Xavier Vignon arrived in the region in 1996, and started to make wines here in 1998. He was an outsider,
content:
Xavier Vignon arrived in the region in 1996, and started to make wines here in 1998. He was an outsider, but it was standing above the village of Suzette, looking across to the Dentelles, where he decided he wanted to be a consultant winemaker focusing on the Rhône.

He is also one of the co-presidents of the Beaumes de Venise Cru. He took me to the spot high up in the cru where he looked over the vineyards back in 1996 and decided that this was the place for him.

Xavier made his name as a consultant, and his own wine project was born more-or-less by accident. During his consulting work, he took a little wine from each cru, just enough to make a small bottling (5000 litres = 1 pallet = 50 cases of 12). ‘This was my unit,’ he says. The idea was to demonstrate how good southern Rhône wines could be: back then, their quality wasn’t appreciated as much as it is now. He didn’t want to sell the wines, but rather he aimed to give them away.

But some friends of his submitted two bottles of each to the 2000 edition of the Guide Hachette, some 6 wines or so from each of 20 producers. They all ended up in the guide, and one from Ventoux got a coup du Coeur. His personal address in Barroux and his phone number was published in the guide, and it said that he was open 7 days a week (mistakenly; he wasn’t even selling wine). And people started turning up. ‘It became a nightmare!’ he says. But he registered as a negociant and began selling bottle by bottle.

Now he’s begun buying vineyards, too. This began when he sold his analysis laboratory in 2012. His focus is on Beaumes-de-Venise with 16 hectares, but he also has vineyards in Vaqueyras, Ventoux and Châteauneuf, with 37 hectares overall.

Xavier has some really interesting ideas, one of which is the Vinarium.

This is a large tank of 7000 litre capacity that acts like a sort of wine womb. Inside it, Xavier fits five 200 litre barrels, with stainless steel hoops and fittings (so they don’t corrode). He now has 10 Vinariums. Interestingly, there are two different sorts of Vinarium wine: the wine inside the barrels, and then the wine around the barrels – the amniotic fluid, if you like. I tried one white wine that was this latter category: it finishes fermentation in the tank (it goes to the Vinarium at 1030 density).

He’s also tried this with amphorae. He has one wine, a Châteauneuf-du-Pape, that he has aged for 6 years using this immersion process.

The story of how he devised the concept for the Vinarium is convoluted but interesting.

When he was running the analysis laboratory in conjunction with his consultancy work, he noticed that a lot of the tannins from the 2003 vintage reds were very dry. This was the very hot year, a couple of decades before almost all years were very hot. What could be done about these dry tannins?

In 2007 when he was consulting for Château La Nerthe, they tasted the 2003 and compared it with the new 2007 wine. The 2003 was tasting very dry, but the 2007 was tasting beautiful. The analysis was the same. He was trying to find a way to make the 2003 better: was there a way to soften those dry tannins?

Then, one night, he remembered an experience from 1988 when he was working in Saint-Emilion. He’d fined 400 barrels with albumin, but when he came back two weeks later and sampled the barrels, the tannins were still very dry. He didn’t understand why.

Then the old cellarmaster came in, drunk. He says that wines with hard tannins like these had happened many times, and the problem was caused by forgetting to add salt to the albumin. He added a gram of salt per hectolitre, and it was like a miracle.

So Xavier got up and went to the winery at 3 am in the morning, added 1 g salt/hectolitre in a bench trial. It was too much. But 0.2 g/hl worked like a treat. The hard tannins in the 2003 resolved, but salt isn’t a legal addition to wine, so he couldn’t say how he had turned the wines around.

He found a work around that was legal. The 2007 had much higher levels of mineral salts. Fives times as much. Adding 2007 to 2003 resolved the tannins. He published some studies on minerals and saltiness and their effect on tannins.

Xavier also did an examination of ageing barrels of wine in the sea. If there’s any exchange between the wine and the sea, then the wine is undrinkable. With wine in the sea, though, the oxidation process turned out to be much slower.

His sea immersion experiments were ended when he got in trouble with the customs, who fined him. His next trial was bringing the sea into the winery: he immersed barrels of wine in concrete tanks, but the concrete didn’t like the salt water.

This is where Xavier realised that it’s just liquid, and wine is a liquid. So this is where he began ageing barrels in wine, after changing the hoops to stainless steel from iron.

Xavier Vignon Extra Côtes du Rhône Blanc NV France
12.5% alcohol. This is a blend of three vintages of wine aged in the Vinarium, bottled in 2025. Grenache Blanc, Clairette, Piquepoul Blanc and Marsanne. 18 months on lees with low SO2, 24 months in Vinarium. This is really fresh and linear with lovely texture and good acidity. Pear, citrus fruit, pure and linear with great precision. Really interesting. 94/100

Xavier Vignon Beaumes-de-Venise 2022 France
15% alcohol. Aromatic, fine and pure with juicy red cherry and redcurrant fruit as well as fine spices. This is really elegant, wearing its alcohol well. Has real finesse, tending to elegance. 93/100

Xavier Vignon Arcane L’Etoile Beaumes de Venise NV France
15% alcohol. No vintage declared on this wine. Elegant and slightly peppery with layered cherry, strawberry and plum fruit. Rounded, with a bit of spicy framing and some silkiness, but also a bit of structure on the finish. Very stylish and quite intriguing. 93/100

Xavier Vignon Arcane L’Impératrice 2023 Gigondas, France
Warm, spicy, textural and elegant with strawberries and cherries, as well as some red fruit. Such precision and purity. 94/100

Xavier Vignon Muscat de Beaumes de Venise 2024
15% alcohol. Nice depth here with some layers of spice interweaving with the textured pear and grape notes. Rich but in balance, finishing sweet. 92/100

Video: touring around the cru with Xavier Vignon”

title: Beaumes-de-Venise exploration: Petitjean family, Domaine de Cassan and Château Les Croix des Pins
summary: Websites: https://domainedecassan.fr https://www.chateaulacroixdespins.fr Domaine de Cassan is a beautifully located estate at the foot of the Dentelles de Montmirail. I
content:
Websites: https://domainedecassan.fr https://www.chateaulacroixdespins.fr

Domaine de Cassan is a beautifully located estate at the foot of the Dentelles de Montmirail. I met with proprietor Jérôme Petitjean to hear the story and taste through the wines. As with many local domaines, he’s not restricted to just one cru, but has vineyards in three. As well as 4 hectares in Beaumes-de-Venise, he’s got 25 hectares in Ventoux and 7 in Gigondas.

The Domaine was established in the 1970s, and until recently was owned by the Croset family. In 2010 the Petitjean family took over running their vineyards in Gigondas and Beaumes-de-Venise, and converted them to organics. Two years ago they took over the domaine in its entirety. They are in the process of renovating the rest of the vineyards, where he says he’s got a lot of work to do.

The Petitjeans are originally from Epernay, and still have 5 hectares of vines in Champagne, as well as a two other domaines in Vaucluse: Croix des Pins and Domaine des Nymphes.

Château Croix des Pins also has some vineyards in Beaumes-de-Venise.

Domaine de Cassan Le Couer des Dentelles Beaumes-de-Venise 2024 France
15% alcohol. This is the main cuvée with 90% Grenache and 10% Syrah from vines at 400 m in clay/limestone soils. Aged in concrete tanks. This is supple and fine with sweet cherry and berry fruits, some silkiness and a hint of green. Easy and expressive. Fine-grained structure with lovely precision, carrying the alcohol well. 93/100

Château La Croix des Pins Les Contreforts de Montmirail 2024 Beaumes-de-Venise, France
15% alcohol. 80% Grenache, 20% Syrah, aged in concrete egg. There’s some nice black pepper and black cherry character here with sleek black cherry and blackberry fruit on the palate. This also has some saltiness and fine-grained structure. Fresh and expressive. 93/100

Domaine de Cassan Félibrige 2020 Beaumes-de-Venise, France
15% alcohol. 50% Grenache, 50% Syrah. Oak aged. Made by the former owner. This is rich, vivid and spicy with some tannic structure under the cherry fruit, with notes of liquorice and spice, as well as hints of pepper and olives. 93/100

Domaine de Cassan Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise 2024 France
15% alcohol. Fruity and aromatic with appealing grapey richness, and notes of pear and peach. There’s some melon, too. Lovely weight here: quite delicious. 93/100

title: Beaumes-de-Venise exploration: Domaine De Fenouillet
summary: Website: https://domaine-fenouillet.fr/ I visited with Justine and Valentin Soard, who are cousins. Domaine de Fenouillet was created in 1989 by
content:
Website: https://domaine-fenouillet.fr/

I visited with Justine and Valentin Soard, who are cousins. Domaine de Fenouillet was created in 1989 by Justine’s father, and Vincent arrived two years later. They have 35 hectares of vines, split over 8 communes, which have been farmed organically since 2012. We spent some time in the vineyards on the slopes below

Most of the soils here are the Terres Blanches, but they also have some sandy soils, too. As well as Beaumes-de-Venise they also make Ventoux and Vacqueyras.

Domaine de Fenouillet Oversant Blanc 2024 IGP Vaucluse
50% Mucat, 50% Viognier. Fresh and brighy with grapey aromatics showing nice prescision, finishing dry. Lively and bright with some spiciness on the finish. 89/100

Domaine de Fenouillet Beaumes de Venise Yvon Soard 2021
50% Syrah, 40% Grenache, 10% Mourvèdre in the dentelles (7 hectares in Suzette and 2 hectares in Roc Alaric), argile calcaire soils. Destemmed, then concrete tanks. Nice weight and density with sweet cherries and plums. Fleshy, a bit meaty, and spicy with nice definition and some tannin. Has good acidity and brightness. 94/100

Domaine de Fenouillet Quand vin le Soard 2019
40% Syrah, 35% Mourvèdre, 25% Grenache. Don’t make this cuvée every year. Vinified in concrete tank then 18 months in older oak barrels, then another six months in concrete. This is rich and intense with some spicy structure and a bit of grip, showing nice lush fruit. Vivid, dense and quite structural with nice richness, showing lovely depth and a bit of lushness to the fruit. 93/100

Domaine de Fenouillet Muscat de Beaumes de Venise 2024
This is rich and intense with pear and peach fruit as well as table grapes, showing nice melony richness and a hint of mint. Rich and quite intense, but stays fresh. Lovely fruity depth to this wine. 93/100

Domaine de Fenouillet Terres Blanches Beaumes de Venise 2023
14.5% alcohol. Organic. 50% Grenache, 35% Syrah, 15% Mourvèdre. Bright and with nice energy, but also some meaty, spicy depth. Shows sweet cherry and berry fruit with nice intensity and a bit of grip on the finish. Lots of presence here. 93/100

Domaine de Fenouillet Muscat de Beaumes de Venise Rosé 2025
20% red muscat, macerated for a few hours in the press. Pale pink colour. Lively, bright and fruity with some mandarin and a touch of cherry with sweetness but also freshness. Has a delicious presence to it, showing some complexity but with the emphasis firmly on the fruit. 93/100

Domaine de Fenouillet Muscat de Beaumes de Venise Rouge 2025
This is really distinctive with some spice from skin maceration (8-10 days), as well as a bit of cherry fruit. So expressive and nicely complex, with sweetness as well as fruitiness and a bit of structure. Quite refined with a hint of almond and liquourice, finishing fresh. Very stylish. 94/100

Domaine du Fenouillet Muscat de Beaumes de Venise Sélection Ancestrale 2023
15% alcohol. 10% red Muscat. Full golden colour. Complex, spicy and layered with lovely depth, a hint of structure, and nice apple, pear and table grape characters. Good concentration and depth here, showing real interest. 94/100

title: The brilliant Douro wines of Mateus Nicolau de Almeida/Ameztoy & Almeida
summary: Website: https://ameztoyalmeida.com/ Mateus Nicolau de Almeida is the son of the well known João Nicolau d’Almeida of Ramos Pinto fame,
content:
Website: https://ameztoyalmeida.com/

Mateus Nicolau de Almeida is the son of the well known João Nicolau d’Almeida of Ramos Pinto fame, and the grandson of Fernando Nicolau d’Almeida who began Barca Velha back in 1952.

Growing up surrounded by wine he went out and got lots of experience around the world of wine, including an important time spent working on the Bordeaux properties of Denis Dubourdieu, the famous wine scientist. In 1996 he was working at Cantenac Brown, another Bordeaux estate, where he met his wife, Teresa Ameztoy.

Like Mateus, Teresa has a winemaking family background. Her father worked for La Rioja Alta, and she worked as chief winemaker at Ramos Pinto from 2005-2019, and now they both work together on the venture that Mateus began in 2014, after he left Muxagat, a winery he founded in 2003.

They have 4 hectares of organically farmed vineyards, and also source grapes from other growers.

Mateus Nicolau de Almeida Mater-Dôme (Mêda) Branco 2024 Douro, Portugal
Aged in a mix of concrete and 500 litre barrels. Lovely energy here. Bright and mineral with fine spices. Has nice citrus density and also some richer grapey notes. 93/100

Mateus Nicolau de Almeida Eremitas Antão do Desserto 2022 Douro, Portugal
Rabigato raised in concrete, after foot treading for 3 hours. Bold, mineral and spicy with nice density, and a bit of grip. Very stylish with nice weight. 93/100

Mateus Nicolau de Almeida Curral Teles Vinho Vermelho NV Douro, Portugal
A blend of 2020 and 2021, 3 hours foot treading then pressed. Nicely textured with sweet, smooth cherry and plum fruit. A lovely layered lighter red wine that’s soft and expressive. 93/100

Mateus Nicolau de Almeida Trans-Douro-Express Baixo Corgo 2022 Douro, Portugal
Aromatic with lovely sweet cherry and plum fruit. Some raspberry, too. Chalky and fine and fresh. 95/100

Mateus Nicolau de Almeida Curral Teles Tinto 2015 Douro, Portugal
This is stainless steel only. Rich but fresh, with lovely texture and finesse. Structured and broad but with real finesse. 95/100

Mateus Nicolau de Almeida Mater-Dôme (Mêda) 2009 Douro, Portugal
2 years in oak/concrete then 13 years in stainless steel. Fine and layered, spicy and dense, with a little evolution but lovely detail. Grippy and refined. 95/100

title: Sablière: a new 0% alcohol sparkling ‘wine’ designed from first principles
summary: Website: https://sabliere.co.uk/ I’ve written quite a bit about the attempts to make interesting, complex dealcoholized wines. There’s another approach, which
content:
Website: https://sabliere.co.uk/

I’ve written quite a bit about the attempts to make interesting, complex dealcoholized wines. There’s another approach, which is purpose-built proxies: complex non-wine drinks that operate in the same space as wine.

And this week I met up with Lucy Isles, co-owner of a new brand, Sablière, which is built from the ground up after a lot of research to behave just like a good Champagne or sparkling wine.

Lucy emphasizes that this is not a sparkling tea or a kombucha, but something that has been put together after a lengthy research journey.

Her partner in this venture is Kim Wilson, who studied brewing technology at Heriot Watt University, and then worked for Diageo. Sablière is made in their own facility in Edinburgh.

The challenge they faced is one that’s common to anyone working in the zero alcohol space. Without alcohol, they have no viscosity, no sterility, no mouthfeel and no texture.

She describes the research journey as a ‘wonderful multidisciplinary experience’.

They have worked with innovative South African winemaker Bruce Jack, with a microbiologist from Lallemand in Denmark, an Edinburgh University physicist looking at bubbles, and Andrew Gardner, a tea specialist (a tea specialist).

‘We were really trying to think, how can we do something novel here?’ says Lucy.

So, their first pair of sparkling wines are now live. These are meant to be wine replacements, and they are beginning to look at how they can also do this with still white and red wines.

The wines are built up using four key ingredients. There’s tea, which gives length. There are apples, for body. Honey gives aroma. And, finally, verjus gives acidity. They finish by carbonating to 6 bars pressure, the same as Champagne.

There are two expressions so far. One is a Blanc de Blancs style, which they based on Ruinart, and the other is a rosé based on Charles Heidsieck.

The Blanc is a blend of white teas, and they worked with tea sommelier Joyce Maina to select these. There are white curls from Nepal, and white peony from China. They extract the teas in house, using a different process for each. The verjus is from Sussex, which adds viscosity and acidity, and this is balanced with malic acid from cox apples. They use a range of yeasts from Lallemand to give some wine-like qualities, but this fermentation produces no alcohol.

One key decision was to go for 0.0% alcohol rather than 0.5% because of the Middle East market.

The final element is blossom honey distillate, adding sweetness but not sugary weight. Altogether the Blanc and Rosé have 37 g/l sugar. So they are sterile filtered. There are no added sulfites, but some sulfites are used by the verjus producer: they are looking to see whether they could eliminate these sulfites too.

What does it taste like? It has lovely aromas: fruity, herby and aromatic with some honeyed notes, floral elements and a touch of green. The palate is fresh and textured and you get the honey and tea notes, but also nice fruitiness and good acidity. Very stylish and fruit driven.

The rosé has Kentish kiss apples which give some pink notes. Four teas are used: mountain oolong (smoky, oxidized notes), gold curl, wild lapsang and da hong pao (delicate caramel).

It’s a golden colour with a slight pink hue. There’s a fruity, herby note on the nose with red apple, mandarin and dried herbs. In the mouth there’s nice bite with some structure and good acidity, and nice herby complexity. There’s even a slight caramel twist. This is really good.

I wouldn’t mistake either for Champagne, but these are high quality, intentional sparkling ‘wines’ that are quite friendly and offer a bit of complexity. Sablière are selling direct to customers at £32 for the Blanc and £35 for the Rosé. They launched quietly in January, their website was launched in April, and they already have 20 clients (restaurants and retail).

title: Highlights: the chillable Olivier Coste Bisou Rouge 2025
summary: This is great: a delicious, drinkable Languedoc red designed to be drunk chilled. Olivier Coste Bisou Rouge 2025 Pays d’Oc,
content:
This is great: a delicious, drinkable Languedoc red designed to be drunk chilled.

Olivier Coste Bisou Rouge 2025 Pays d’Oc, France
11.5% alcohol. This is designed to be served chilled, and the lips on the front label change from red to blue when it’s at the right temperature. It’s a lighter-style red with low tannins, but it’s still a red wine. Lovely floral, sappy, sweet cherry and berry fruits, and nice weight on the palate. Crunchy and delicious; fruity and enjoyable. There’s a touch of sweetness and it is juicy and easy, but satisfying. Really impressive. 91/100
